hero.title: Seating Arrangement
hero.description: Seating Arrangement is a high-scoring and critical component of the General Intelligence and Reasoning section in the Allahabad High Court RO/ARO and UPPSC examinations. It evaluates a candidate's analytical capability, spatial orientation, and ability to process complex multi-variable conditional data under strict time constraints.

cards.details: Introduction of simple single-row arrangements focusing on absolute positions (e.g., 'A is sitting second to the left of B').
Inclusion of circular tables with mixed inward and outward facing directions, increasing the difficulty of left-right determinations.
Integration of additional parameters like professions, favorite colors, or departments along with seating positions.

mnemonics.title: Seating Arrangement Mnemonics & Study Tricks
mnemonics.description: Quick memory triggers to recall key facts for AHC RO/ARO exams.

items.title: FLAC - Facing Left Anti-Clockwise
items.decryption: Remember that when facing the center of a circular table, moving Left means moving Anti-Clockwise.

items.title: S-N-R (South North Reverse)
items.phrase: South means Reverse your Normal Right-Left
items.decryption: In South-facing linear arrangements, always reverse your standard Right and Left assumptions.

flashcards.title: Active Recall Flashcards
flashcards.description: Hover or click to reveal the answers. Revisit these cards to build instant recall.

items.question: In a circular table facing the center, if person X is sitting to the immediate right of Y, which direction is X relative to Y?
How many total arrangements exist for 5 persons sitting in a single straight line?
What does the statement 'A sits third to the right of B' mean in an unclosed circular arrangement of 8 persons?
items.answer: There are exactly 2 persons sitting between B and A when counted from B's right.

items.question: If 6 persons sit in a row facing South, who sits at the extreme left if person 'P' is at the conventional extreme right?
items.answer: For South-facing rows, the viewer's left is the persons' right, so P's position must be carefully re-evaluated based on individual seating coordinates.

traps.title: Common Exam Traps to Avoid
items: The 'And' vs. 'Who' Confusion: In statements like 'A is third to the right of B who is second to the left of C', 'who' refers to the immediately preceding person (B). If it used 'and' ('A is third to the right of B and second to the left of C'), 'and' refers to the first subject (A).
Ignoring Outward Facing Left-Right Reversal: Aspirants often apply inward-facing rules automatically to outward-facing circular arrangements, leading to entirely inverted position calculations.

Assuming Linear Ends are Fixed Without Proof: Assuming a person sits at an extreme end simply because their relative position is given can destroy the entire matrix. Wait for explicit 'extreme end' phrasing.
